body.hook: In Mandarin, the syllable "ma" can mean "mother," "hemp," "horse" or "scold," depending only on the tone of your voice. Say it the wrong way and "my mother" could become "my horse"! Tones are the key to being understood in Mandarin.

vocabulary.definition: The system that writes Chinese sounds with the Latin alphabet.
Tone: the pitch pattern of a syllable.
Neutral tone: light and short, with no tone mark (ma).

study.title: The Tone Ladder
study.question: How do tones change meaning in Mandarin?
study.passage:
The four tones on "ma":
• mā 妈 = mother (1st tone: high and flat, like singing a long note)
• má 麻 = hemp (2nd tone: rising, like asking "What?")
• mǎ 马 = horse (3rd tone: dips low then rises, like "Hmm?" when unsure)
• mà 骂 = scold (4th tone: sharp drop, like a firm "No!")
• ma 吗 = question word (neutral tone: light and short)
Hand signals: draw each tone in the air with your hand as you say it.
Sentence: 妈妈骂马吗？Māma mà mǎ ma? = Is Mom scolding the horse?
Tone change (sandhi): when two third tones come together, the first one changes to a second tone. 你好 is written nǐ hǎo but said "ní hǎo."
Activity 1, Tone ladder (10 minutes): The teacher says a syllable; students show 1, 2, 3 or 4 fingers.
Activity 2, Tone pairs (10 minutes): With a partner, say and identify: bā (eight) / bà (dad); shī / shí (shí = ten); mǎi (buy) / mài (sell).
Activity 3, Greet with tones: 你好！nǐ hǎo (hello), 谢谢 xièxie (thank you), 再见 zàijiàn (goodbye).
